turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that he would ensure O-lan’s last wishes were fulfilled and that their son would be well-guided by him and his own father.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling nervous and deeply respectful, told his mother that he would follow her wishes and his father’s guidance.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she needed to see her eldest son married before she could rest, her voice carrying an urgent yet weary tone.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would arrange the marriage as she wished and that their son would be well cared for.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, his voice trembling slightly, told his mother that he would do everything in his power to honour her wishes and make her proud.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid, noticing O-lan’s weakened state, quietly told her that all preparations for the eldest son’s marriage would be made swiftly and with care.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she felt the weight of her illness but was comforted by their dedication to fulfilling her wishes.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, his voice trembling with emotion, told his mother and father that he was ready to marry as soon as possible to ease her worries.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would make sure everything was arranged for the eldest son’s marriage and that she should rest, knowing her wishes would be fulfilled.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would ensure the preparations were perfect, giving O-lan peace of mind.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she felt the urgency to see her eldest son married, knowing her time was short and her peace of mind depended on the fulfillment of this wish.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would ensure the eldest son’s marriage would be a grand and joyous affair, a reminder that her legacy and love would live on.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother and father that he would do everything in his power to make her happy, including preparing for the marriage as quickly as possible.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she felt the urgency of her wish growing stronger with each passing day, urging them to hasten the preparations so she could rest with a clear heart.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan and Wang Lung that she would oversee the arrangements personally, ensuring that every detail was attended to with care and promptness.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she would rest easier knowing they were doing all they could to prepare for the marriage, urging them to focus on the happiness of the union rather than on grandeur.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid assured O-lan and Wang Lung that she understood their wishes, promising to keep the preparations simple yet warm, focusing on the happiness of the union.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan and the others that he would make sure the preparations were carried out swiftly and with all the love they deserved, assuring her that her wishes would be fulfilled and her son would find happiness in marriage.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told O-lan and Wang Lung that he would do everything in his power to make the marriage a source of joy for his mother, expressing his gratitude for their efforts and his determination to bring happiness to their household.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her family that she felt a sense of peace knowing her son was committed to making the marriage a source of joy, and she urged them to focus on the essence of the union rather than external displays of wealth.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
